Well, the size and shape and even the color of these fenders are just right on our off white pier. They fit perfectly (placed horizontally) and look great!
I'm thinking of buying another set so that it goes farther along the pier and has a more streamlined look.

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can I'm buying calories. I am buying calories to tuck away for use after all other calories have been consumed. I have this and know it is available. I dont need to worry about it. It is there as part of my "calorie savings account". Not worried about taste, not worried about anything other than calories- preferably a variety of flavors with a good ratio of macros (fat, protein, carbohydrates). Emergency food is what it is, and what it will be. With increasing prices, todays caloric purchase is a savings over tomorrows.

So no, I haven't tried it. I HAVE used other Augason Farms products for daily life use and have been pleased. I regularly buy Augason Farms (best price point, best sales). I have tried those items only because the sale price was better than buying non emergency packed food items. I use a lot of tomato powder, dehydrated vegetables, protein crumbles, etc.. and once in awhile a sale will work in my favor. That is when I will buy 2 of something. One for now, one for way later. Rinse and repeat.

Certain food items have at least 25 year shelf life, some items are 10 years. No matter, I will eat it all 30 years down the line if need be. Foods dont just go "bad". The date is not a safety issue. It is a quality issue. So maybe the smell, taste, texture, or vitamin content alters a little over time, but it is still edible. Calories are still there.

If you want to be sure of a tasty meal that is within the best by date range, then simple stack your pantry with foods that you know and love. Rotate. Have a "working pantry" that you grab from on a daily basis, then have a "storage pantry" that works as your own in home "store". It also serves as your emergency preps. When you need to pull from your storage pantry, be sure to replace. Keep adding to it, one or two cans at a time. one or two bags of something at a time. Emergency food does not need to be emergency packaged food (prices are higher for the packaging, uniformity, processing etc). If "emergency" packaged food is outside your budget, then dont bother. If it is something you are keen on, then look for sales regularly (maybe daily) and buy when the good price strikes. Of course, you can look into creating your own long term storage meals too (mylar, oxy absorbers, pails, etc).

Just.. have something. Dont be someone who has bare shelves and scoffs at preparedness because emergency meals taste bad. Nah, buy what is good to you, buy what is affordable to you, buy basic stuff or buy fancy emergency stuff. But have stuff. Prices aren't coming down, prices will continue to go up, food will be harder to come by. So at the very least consider it an investment. And if there is a true need for it in terms of *vaguely gestures around* all else that is going on (weather events, political events, ww3, etc) then you wont be scrambling, begging off neighbors, stealing, etc.

So current $60 for nearly 20,000 calories of a variety of food? Not too shabby in light of everything. (same $60 can buy a lot more calories, but be sure to store well for max "freshness").
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can

It also tracks how many flights of stairs I've climbed, as well as tracking individual workouts, number of active minutes daily, and other stats. I get an email every week with a summary of my activity. It syncs with an app that I use to track caloric intake.

I've set mine up to alert me to phone calls and it has an alarm function. Both have really come in handy.

The only drawback so far (and it's not the fault of the Fitbit) is that I think I'm a little too aware of how little sleep I'm getting! It tells you how long you've slept, how many minutes you were restless and how many times you woke up. Am I really only getting about 5 hours of sleep a night? No wonder I'm tired.

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker Well.  I have been using this for many months.  I waited to be provide a fair and honest assessment. This is a review of my personal experience.  My main disappointment is the syncing with the fitbit app - I have a samsung android smart phone with the app installed, further - the app is current with all provided updates. The fitbit 3 itself needs to be "restarted" multiple times a week- you must attach it to the charging cable, push/hold the side button and hold for up to 10 seconds to force restart.  Otherwise it does NOT sync.  SUPER annoying.  And then there are the times when it randomly decides NOT to record my sleep record.  GRRRR....  I have had multiple fitbits - beginning with their gen one version.  Provides reasonably accurate info - BUT if you must FIGHT to get the info through sync - it sort of looses it appeal.  While it says that it does allow you to swim, so water friendly, I do not soak or submerge the fitbit.  I don't remove it as I wash dishes or my hands - so it has been splashed with water.  When I get in the pool, I take it off.  I just don't trust the water friendly part.  I may go back to my fitbit 2 because it is so much more slim and attractive.  These are somewhat clunky.  I also have tried the much larger watch face version - I quickly stopped using it as it is horribly uncomfortable in size alone - the fitbit 3 is much better than that watch face/square version.  The bands on the fitbit 3 are easy to change.  I have not placed a screen/face protection shields on and haven't had too much trouble with scratching - in fact I don't see any - yet.  So I can't say how easy it is to replace the face - or to place the protection screening on.  I wear my fitbit on one wrist during the day and change it to the other wrist at night while sleeping - I use an alcohol wipe to clean the back of the unit and band several times a week. Further I don't wear it one or two nights a week to give my skin a break and to charge it.  I did purchase the perforated (holes in the band) to provide more breathability.  It is a workable step monitor.  I just wish it would sync more reliably and without forcing a restart which you can't just do where ever you are - but must be done while attached to the charging cord.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and I hope this info was helpful to you in some way.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

Goplus Fitness Hyper Extension Hyperextension Bench Chair Workout Core Abdominal My official review on YouTube is a 3.5 but half stars don't fly on Amazon. For a video version check this out: https://youtu.be/abd0bJ7ZMiQ

Pros:
-Cost.
-Shipping speed.
-Quality with cost factored in.
-Works well for home gym purposes.

Cons:
-Awful instructions.
-Adjustability is limited.
-Light commercial would be a stretch based on the design of the ankle supports.

The cons are a bit strong because the instructions are not step by step. It's basically a build sheet so some trial and error will occur when assembling. The bolts are not clearly labeled/defined so deciphering between them is somewhat of a guess. Other than the ankle support and adjustability this could be light commercial but the ankle support is very wobbly. The adjustability is limited as well even for a hyperextension (I'm 5'8" and use the closest notch). To do GHRs I'd have to drill a few more holes around 4 inches closer.

Overall it's a solid buy and I'd recommend its purchase based on the price. I've had the lower prices Roman chair on Amazon (around $65) and it was much more lightweight than this.
text_fidelity_b: Goplus Fitness Hyper Extension Hyperextension Bench Chair Workout Core Abdominal

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Ultra Running Hydration Belt, 17oz This is a great minimalist running belt, I generally hate running with anything that weighs me down or impedes my running form. I'm a fast middle distance runner (ie 10k up to half marathon) so I typically don't need a ton of gels/water like those running full marathon and longer distances. I prefer to run without a belt/vest if possible.. but this is the best hydration solution I've tried in terms of being minimal, breathable and not impeding my running form very much.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it does run a bit snug and can be difficult to pull on if you are in between the size ranges but I believe this is intended to keep the belt secure from bouncing around. I have a 31 inch waist and 36 inch hips, Camelbak lists the S/M as being for 28-32 waist and 30-35 for the M/L size so I am between sizes but I think the S/M was the right call because the larger size would probably bounce around too much.

My one complaint with this belt is that I wish there were more pockets with secure closure. There is one zippered pocket and all the rest of the pockets just have elastic at the top to prevent items from spilling out (and a drawsting/cinch for the rear water flask pocket). The key pocket does have a clip to prevent your keys from falling out which is nice but I wish the side pockets had a snap closure or something because I have had items fly out when I was trail running and jumping down ledges.

Overall, this is a great belt and I would recommend it for those looking for a minimalist solution.. the included flask only holds 17 oz so its not a ton of water but if you hate running with heavy hydration gear then this is a great solution.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Ultra Running Hydration Belt, 17oz

text_fidelity_a:
Heated Glove Liners for Women Men, Rechargeable Heated Gloves Touchscreen Hand Warmers for Work Ski Fishing Hunting by V.Step I've been eyeballing some heated gloves for a while. I have bad issues with my finger joints and heat helps, but heating pads or rice bags are big and bulky and make my hands useless while being warmed. When I saw these heated liners/gloves, I thought they might be a good option, even though they are pretty pricy.
These are definitely on the thin size (which is what I was looking for). I got mediums which fit my hand like a ...er...glove. They do have touch-screen conductivity pad things on the thumbs and index fingers, which seem to work just fine. They only heat on the top side-no heading on the palm side of the glove. They get warm, not hot, when on alone. Much warmer if you have something over them, so if you are using these as liners, they should keep your hands toasty. Three heat settings and long press on/off to prevent accidental button pressing. They lasted for about 3 hours on high heat for me.
The batteries must be removed from the gloves to be charged. Comes with a special split charger so you can charge both, and they are fully charged in about three hours. The battery is a bit bulky and goes on the palm-side of the wrist which is a bit of a bummer for me since I want to use them while I work.
Decently thin, so I can wear them while working/typing/crocheting. Thin enough to easily wear under another pair of gloves if you are going outside on a chilly morning, which you will probably need to do. I did wear these out once and while I could tell they were warm they didn't really keep my hands warm when out in the elements. I did not have another pair of gloves on top so I suspect that would have made a difference.
I'm quite happy with these as a heated joint relief while working option. Had I bought them for keeping my hands warm outside I'm not sure I would be as pleased, especially for the three digit price tag they currently are listed for.
text_fidelity_b: Heated Glove Liners for Women Men, Rechargeable Heated Gloves Touchscreen Hand Warmers for Work Ski Fishing Hunting by V.Step

text_fidelity_a:
Rquite Female Urination Device, Female Urinal Silicone Funnel Urine Cups Portable Urinal Standing Up to Pee Funnel for Travelling, Camping, Hiking, Outdoor Activities -Carrying Bag Included (2 Packs) I have had some issues in the past after a car accident. In order for my legs to feel better and out of pain, I need to go walking. In order to go walking, I had to find a place to urinate in the woods if I needed to. The problem is that one time I got stuck squatting and I could not get up. It was embarrassing and frustrating. I remember saying to my husband that if I could stand and do what he did, maybe I could walk again. I really didn't think that was possible, but..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
These two urinals come exactly as pictured with the listing. There is a faux leather bag with a drawstring that will fit one of them.

HOW TO USE
This has to be pressed up into yourself and then aimed forward. The key is to control the urine flow so that it does not come out so fast, it overflows. It will project outward away from the body until it reaches a trickle, then you may have some issues with it dropping straight down. Prepare for that when you use it.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
I have to say it takes a bit of practice, but this really does help a LOT. I also like it if I need to go to the bathroom and the seat is dirty or even if there is a urinal in it, I can use that. The only problem is wiping. My solution to that is keeping wipes in packets with the urinal so that I can clean afterward.

IMPORTANT NOTE
I keep a zipper closure plastic bag inside the carry bag. That way if I have to use this urinal and I can not get to water to clean it right away, it won't smell and soil the carry bag.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great invention. It is soft, easy to use, and with practice convenient. I do wish this came with TWO carry bags instead of just one, however.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. Despite wishing there were two carry bags, I do think this is a great invention. It has helped me out and now I can go walking with confidence and get my legs to get better again.
text_fidelity_b: Rquite Female Urination Device, Female Urinal Silicone Funnel Urine Cups Portable Urinal Standing Up to Pee Funnel for Travelling, Camping, Hiking, Outdoor Activities -Carrying Bag Included (2 Packs)

But otherwise they are about the same.

I'm female and the cage inside the large/x-large glove fits my hand very well. I would use these gloves for cardio-kickboxing only as they are not meant to actually use to box with. You will need gloves made for that. These will serve as sparring gloves too. They appear to be well constructed and should last a long time if used properly and taken care of. The large velcro strip around the wrists make for a very secure, snug fit. And though the palm of these gloves have 5 small holes for ventilation, I am quite sure your hands will get sweaty after some time spent in them.

These are excellent, especially for the price. the red and white colors are quite nice to look at also.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling The saddle bag is a decent, basic product that suits its purpose. Here are some specific points:
Size: You have the dimensions, so you know the size. It’s tapered from top to bottom, so that’s something to consider beyond just the dimensions. It’s not a commuter bag—not its intent—and so its size is more than suitable I’d say for those little things you might want to carry with you on a ride: you phone, keys, whatever you carry money in (for those who still carry money). You can fit a tube and tool set in for peace of mind, but that will obviously reduce room for those other things depending on their size.

Form: as mentioned, it’s tapered toward the bottom so it fits against the bike under the seat. It’s pretty long, so you’ll want to make sure it will fit under the seat—I can see some bikes not having space for it depending on how high their seat is raised (mine is just on the edge of this being a good fit). Same is true if you have a rack over your back wheel (for panniers)—it’s so long that there’s a decent chance it will overlap the rear part of the rack. It is flexible enough to crunch down and reduce its footprint, but obviously then you’ve ust lost some of its total space.

There’s a small mesh pocket inside to keep something separate (in other words so it doesn’t just mix in the large space, making it easier for instance to grab your keys instead of fishing around). It’s a decent solution but I would have preferred if it had also zipped.

Construction: it seems solidly built enough. The material appears pretty tough, as if it will handle wear and tear well, along with the elements. I’m not sure about how it will do with rain (at least not yet). I don’t get a sense (and there was no documentation) that it is water “proof”, but my guess would be it is at least somewhat water “resistant” based on the feel and construction of the material. Personally, until you’ve experienced a good rainfall (we’re in drought conditions here) and can see how it deals, I’d put anything valuable in a plastic bag.

Mounting: Simple and easy. Three straps/loops that give it good stability. Thanks to the three straps and the size, it doesn’t move/shift around at all under my seat.

So a nice little carry-on but definitely check that the length will work for you (especially people with their seat pretty low).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling

GSI Outdoors Percolator Coffee Pot I Glacier Stainless Steel Ultra-Rugged for Brewing Coffee Over Stove and Fire | Ideal for Group Camping, 28 Cup Like most of GSI stuff these pots are made really well. I got the six cup and the fit and finish is very good. I am happy with it.

One really needs to take note of the "cup" capacity of these pots. There are several different definitions of what a fluid "cup" is: 8 fluid ounces, 6 fluid ounces, and 5 fluid ounces. *GSI uses the 5 oz measure.* Thus, the three cup pot will make 15 ounces (3x5=15); the six cup will make 30 ounces, and so on. Actually, a little less when you account for water in the grounds and some evaporation/steam.

My standard ceramic coffee cup takes 10 fluid ounces to fill just below the rim. The smallest coffee star bucks sells is 8 ounces and it's not even on the menu (the smallest on the menu is a `tall' at 12 ounces...just three ounces short of the three cup GSI pot).

I point this out because if you're buying a pot to make coffee for three people who will drink a normal sized cup (or cups) of coffee, you need a larger pot than you might think. Unfortunately, Amazon doesn't show the fluid ounces of each pot.

So, just do the math: __ cups x 5 ounces will tell you what the brewing capacity is and then think about how many ounces you really drink, or plan to brew, and you'll get the right sized pot.
text_fidelity_b: GSI Outdoors Percolator Coffee Pot I Glacier Stainless Steel Ultra-Rugged for Brewing Coffee Over Stove and Fire | Ideal for Group Camping, 28 Cup

After doing some research as to various manufacturers, I decided on Polar since they seem to have the best reputation in the market.

I went with this model mainly because it offered a good set of features without breaking the bank in terms of cost. Plus, it offers the ability (with an add-on docking station: [[ASIN:B004QOW1IU Polar Flowlink]]) to transfer stored data to my PC. I'm not at the point yet where I see a need for that, but down the road I think that may be something I'll use to better analyze workout performance.

I'm especially pleased with the comfort. I've tried straps from lower-end HRMs from Timex and Omron, and they were uncomfortable. This strap fits well and doesn't cause any discomfort from rubbing on my skin when working out.

The manual is well-done - I was up and running very quickly. Usage is also straightforward, although I've found it helpful to keep the manual handy to look up how to use some of the features. The wristband fits well and stays in place, and the display is easy to read. Having a backlit display is also handy when using it in the early morning hours or when it's overcast.

So far, I have no complaints!

90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants First of all, i bought this pants not entirely for yoga and thus i picked the one with pockets. I needed a pair of leggings with fleece that i can walk my dog during winter (in California!!). Don't judge me...but i am terrified of the cold. I bought the pants in two sizes, two colors; all with pockets.

FIT:
"M" and "S" fits me perfectly because the material is super stretchy and extremely comfortable. I'm 5'6 and 133lbs. "M" has the length that would wrap around the heel nicely and it doesn't feel bulky. I ended up taking the "S" simply because it was in black and i didn't want to take the trouble of returning. But on the hindsight, i would have preferred the "M" so i can pull it over my heel and not worry about wearing out the material over time.

COMFORT:
The fleece is very smooth and comfy. Definitely not a thin legging that you can wear underneath a pair of skinny jeans (unfortunately!). The pockets do add on the extra thickness.

WARMTH:
In an evening of ~50F, wearing just the leggings, socks and a pair of running shoes still left my feet feeling cold (again, don't judge the Californians..it's just me!). I couldn't walk my dog comfortably unless i start jogging to build up the heat. When I swapped my running shoes with a pair of Uggs/boots that gave me more coverage, it helped a lot. I've seen reviews where people would wear it outdoor in the snow under some snow pants... i dont know if I can make the same comparison.

Overall, i just love how comfortable the pants are. Not super expensive but also not as cheap.
text_fidelity_b: 90 Degree By Reflex High Waist Fleece Lined Leggings with Side Pocket - Yoga Pants

VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight Good basic inexpensive sunglasses that block uv400 and are polarized. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Yes I believe these are a good value, have great looks and provide the basics. However, there are others out there for half this price that can provide the same basics but sometimes lack in style and fit.
I would say the glasses are a bit narrow on my face but I like the look and was surprised these were nicer than expected.
text_fidelity_b: VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Bocce Ball Set — 8 All Weather Bocce Balls and 1 Pallino — Beach, Backyard Lawn or Outdoor Party Game — Professional, American, and Starter Set Options I like bocce and I was thrilled to have the opportunity to review this set. I was particularly interested in this set because it is marketed as a “professional” set. As a casual bocce set this is great, but as a professional set it’s out of specifications, by more than a little. Since it is priced as a professional set, it misses the mark, though it is fine for casual and family play.

I decided to do a little digging to see what would designate a bocce set as a “professional” set. According to the Bocce Standards Association (yes, seriously), each ball should be a specific size and weight. Of interest is the weight range: 920g +/- 10g (2 lbs.). That’s a tight range of weights, though for sporting equipment used in professional or tournament play that’s not unusual. I measured all 8 balls on a calibrated scale, set to measure in grams. The lightest ball in my set is 947g, and the heaviest is 1026g (2.25 lbs.). Every single ball is outside of the range. I could see being a little outside of the range, but over 100g is way off. Since the spread between the highest and lowest in my set is about 80g, and the specifications allow for a 20g spread between the extremes, this is not a scale problem. Most players wouldn’t even notice, but that’s not the point.

As a casual set, this is a fine bocce set and should last for years. The balls are solid and made of some form of resin, are consistent in appearance and though do get surface scratches during play and transport (very normal), they’re rugged and should not break, crack or chip unless abused or purposely damaged. The set comes in a nylon carry bag and includes a rule book.

This is a nice casual set, not a professional set. The balls are out of spec which makes it unsuitable for true tournament play. And as a casual set, it’s a bit expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Bocce Ball Set — 8 All Weather Bocce Balls and 1 Pallino — Beach, Backyard Lawn or Outdoor Party Game — Professional, American, and Starter Set Options

Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead I received this as a free review sample. I am not going to repeat the product specs on this page since the material and unfolded dimensions are provided by the manufacturer. I will give my take on this and reasons why I rated it so highly.

What I especially like is the compact size that it folds to. Out of the box it's only 12.5x4x1 inches, which will fit in a backpack or even in the glove box of most vehicles (especially if you fold it over lengthwise.)

There is a slight chemical odor as soon as you unbox it, so I recommend airing it out before refolding and storing it for actual use. It takes about an hour for the odor to dissipate.

Using it is as simple as placing your valuables inside, folding over the reinforced rib at the top (the mouth) of the bag two or three times, then doubling and using the closure snaps. You are NOT supposed to press the air out because that will provide buoyancy in the event that it falls into water. I am not sure how much weight it will take to achieve negative buoyancy, but partially filled with air it will support a good five pounds and still maintain a degree of positive buoyancy. The key point and why I rated this so highly is I tested it with a towel and a brick and it kept the towel completely dry.

If you camp, boat or spend time at the beach and want to safeguard wallets, phones and tablets, this bag will do the trick.
text_fidelity_b: Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead

I sure hope they do, because this machine does it all.
If you read the posts from others that have bought this, it is VERY true that you DO NOT tighten the screws in the bottom of the platform before they are all in place or thing just will not line up and you will get the job of taking all the bolts and screws back out and starting over, like we had to.

I am really glad we have this machine, the one thing my husband noticed already, is that he had pain in his feet from nerve damage and it would really be painful at times especially at night when he was sleeping but since he has been using the machine this past week he hardly has any pain at all.

text_fidelity_a:
HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700 This tool gets a bad rap, and unfairly, I think. Sure it takes time, but it works fine for the occasional wheel building project or replacement spoke. It's a nice item to have in the tool box for a rainy day when you can't be riding. You can build or repair a wheel instead. Even a bike shop might find one of these handy.

It's fairly simple. The tool mounts in a vise. The three rollers emboss threads in the spoke, rather than cut them. This makes for a stronger spoke. You turn the crank and the rollers "chase" threads up the spoke. When you get the threaded length you want, you turn the crank in reverse to back the rollers off the spoke.

I just used it to thread 36 14-gauge spokes, with no problems at all. (It threads 14 and 15 gauge spokes.)

The keys to using this tool successfully are to generously use cutting oil (or an equivalent), start with a properly chamfered spoke, and make several passes to get the depth of thread you want.

I think one reason this device gets such a bad rap is that people try to make it cut finished threads in one pass. If you tighten down the rollers that much to start, it will be difficult to get a blank spoke to feed into them.

Practice with a few extra spokes first. Chamfer the ends slightly with a file or a grinder.

Open up the Hozan tool's rollers by loosening the adjustment nut, until it will easily "take" a blank spoke and lightly emboss threads. Back the spoke out, tighten the nut a quarter to half turn, and make another pass through. Repeat this until you get threads embossed deeply enough so that a spoke nipple screws on easily for its full length. That will be your final setting.

Now you can back the adjustment nut off a full turn (360 degrees). This is so you can start a blank spoke. Make a first pass through, back the spoke out, tighten the adjustment nut a half turn, pass the spoke through and back out, and tighten it one half turn again for the final pass. Repeat this process for every spoke you want to thread. After a few you'll get into a rhythm and things will go faster. Apply more cutting oil with every spoke.

After every few spokes clean the rollers. I spray them with WD-40 while holding a folded paper towel underneath, then re-oil them for the next spoke.

The instructions say that with proper care this tool will last for years. I don't see any reason why it won't.
text_fidelity_b: HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700

Extremus Rendu Soft Cooler, 12/20/30 Can Updated Insulated Cooler Bag, Portable and Waterproof Beach Cooler with 100% Leakproof Zipper, Large Capacity for Fishing, Kayaking, Camping, Beaches & Trips We buy our milk from a special farmer that only does grass fed milk. It is not too bad usually, except in the summer, it is tough to keep the milk cold as we go to and from the farm as it is not near our home. This cooler answers that problem.

HOW TO OPEN
This comes with a zipper and an extra pull included. I can see why. This zipper is quite difficult to use. The pack includes a lubrication tube and tells you how to keep the zipper working. Well, I did it several times and it still is not easy to slide the zipper.

INSIDE
The inside is quite a bit smaller than the outside due to the insulation. Our milk bottles will only fit long ways instead of sideways as I thought they would.

DOES IT KEEP THINGS COLD?
I have to say that I got some yogurt the other day and did not have ice to put in the cooler. I put in 3 containers of yogurt which were quart sized. I had them in there for about 5 hours. When I got home, the yogurt was still pretty cold. I am impressed.

STRAPS/HANDLE
The straps and handle on this cooler are really great. The shoulder strap makes it easy for me to carry this along with the other things I have to carry in the house It is comfortable and works out well.

LEAKS?
This did not leak so far when ice melts.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is the perfect cooler for getting our milk this summer. It will allow me to make the trip and not be so concerned about keeping the milk cold in our other coolers because this one with some ice included will work perfectly.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS although the zipper on this is very frustrating and I would like to take off a star, but I don't think it is that bad at this point. I will update of anything changes.

text_fidelity_a:
Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal) --Preamble--

Like many people, I decided to try out some thick bar grips to optimize my current regimen. I too was attracted by the idea of improving my grip and strengthening the whole complex of muscles/tendons/ligaments in my forearms. So I purchased four kinds of wide bar grips - Fat Gripz One (1.75"), Fat Gripz Pro (2.25"), Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips (2"), and Yes4All Thick Bar Grips (2.2").

Before the review, some context:

First, you should ease into these things, and so if you aren't accustomed to thick bar grips, I would recommend you start with the Fat Gripz One. I did not do this; I tried to integrate all four into my routine, and as a result I gave myself acute tendonitis in both arms, in the form of Golfer's Elbow. Now I need to take at least 4 weeks off while I heal up, and no one likes that. I don't think this would have been a problem if I just started with the narrower grips and moved up from there.

Second, if use a ruler, my hand is 6 5/8" (168mm) from the bend of the wrist to the tip of my middle finger. The Fat Grips One is fine, the Iron Bull Strength grips are about the limit of decent grip, and the Fat Grips Pro are too large to get my hand around, limiting me to fairly light dumbbells. For pull-ups, only the Fat Grips one are comfortable, the Iron Bull's are marginal. I have chronic issues with my TFCC (something I was hoping to help alleviate through these grips) and the thicker ones tend to aggravate that complex.

Lastly, I am fairly fit. I am about 183lbs (83.2kg) and was doing sets of 23 pull-ups before this. I could maintain those numbers with the narrower wide grips, but with greater effort. I have my pull-up bar (an Iron Gym) wrapped in racket grip tape, so it is about 1.1" in diameter. Most of my dumbbells have bars that are between 1.1 and 1.25" in diameter.

--Product Review--

The Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 are a respectable alternative to the Fat Gripz. They have a different profile, being more curved in the center, which I don't necessarily prefer, but it isn't really a negative, just different. They are firmer than Fat Gripz, but not much less grippy. I prefer how they look, being all black, no colored logos to distract the eye. As for the scent, they smell like coconut oil to me, which is pleasant.

---Comfort

The Iron Bull Alpha Grips are fairly comfortable, not as much as the Fat Gripz Pro but close. Like other thick bar grips they have a raised pattern pressed into the rubber which give more of an inconsistent surface than an uncomfortable one. The suitability of the raised bump in the middle is going to be highly subjective; I personally like it on dumbbells, but not on my pull-up bar. These have a seam, just like all thick bar grips, though it is smaller than some cheaper models. These don't fit on IronMaster dumbbells due to them having a 1.25" bar, but they fit CAP models and my pull-up bar, an Iron Gym, pretty well. I find the 2" diameter is much nicer to work with than the 2.25" of the Fat Gripz Pro.

---Benefit

Decent benefit, it has an immediately noticeable visual effect, within a week anyway. I had to drop 20% of my reps to compensate, but before the injury I could feel the improvements already, such that it felt odd not to use them. Whereas before the IronMaster bar felt thick, now it feels fairly thin. Definitely helps improve general muscle tone and forearm strength and feels, at least, like the exercises are more engaging. Effect is as described, and I imagine one would see real benefits in muscle mass within a month.

---Conclusion

I'd recommend these as a solid alternative to the Fat Gripz, not necessarily better or worse, but merely different. Presently, I like the Fat Gripz One for pull-ups, the Fat Gripz Pro for light weights (<30lb), and the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 for medium weights (30lb-55lb).
text_fidelity_b: Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal)

text_fidelity_a:
Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz Pointing out a few things brought up in reviews:

1. This is DEHYDRATED zucchini, NOT freeze-dried. Very different methods, different results, different pricing. While Mother Earth does carry some freeze dried, they do not have freeze dried zucchini. Another way to tell? With freeze dried foods, they can be eaten as is (crunchy snack) or rehydrated. Where as with dehydrated foods, most all (except fruits, usually) will need to be rehydrated in order to consume them (too tough to eat). This will require soaking and/or cooking for a period of time. Can't just toss it in the dish you are making and expect it to cook up quickly. So for this, it says to simmer 1 part zucchini to 2 parts water for 10-30 minutes. This very well may take longer. I let it cook for no less than 30 minutes before adding it to what I ultimately want to have it be part of. Another way to get it started is to let soak, then follow up with a shorter simmer.

2. 1/2 cup dried zucchini = 1 cup cooked zucchini. I made up 1/4 cup and it made a very good sized portion. See my pics.

3. End result is NOT EVER going to be same as fresh. Stop that. Then stop blaming the company/brand. YOu will always be disappointed. Best thing to get if you cant get fresh or frozen is to find a company who makes freeze dried. Even then, you are expecting a lot from zucchini. This is similar to others, and there aren't many out there to choose from.

4. Shelf life can be very very long, if not indefinite if stored under proper conditions. Freeze dried for sure, but dehydrated can last a very long time. Be sure to keep it in well sealed container, out of light and dampness. Maybe keep in freezer or further repackaged into mylar or vac sealed jar.

5. Taste is neutral. Kind of like how zucchini can be. I could tell it was zucchini though! I found that with proper rehydration it worked well in adding bulk to tacos, and can always be added to soup. I see it as a nutritional item rather than a way to have a plate of zucchini. Nice way to bulk up meals, add vitamins and minerals, yet not have to rely on fresh (for various reasons). I noticed that the skins were more like late summer yellow squash/zucchini. Kinda reminded me of regular squash- like butternut skins. Not tough but had more "presence" I shall say. DID not taste or feel like "tree bark" in any way.

6. If planning on using it in zucchini bread, muffins, cookies, or sauces, I would recommend running it through the blender after it has been rehydrated. Make it more of a puree. This will impart flavor and decrease any tougher bits.

7. Says processed and packaged in USA, but WHERE do they get their vegetables from?? That I havent seen, here or on their web page

8. If you dont like this packaging, they also offer mylar bag style.

OVERALL: I think it is fine, and it as expected. I love seeing it in my pantry knowing that I have a variety of dehydrated foods to use when I cant get fresh, or food is scarce, or food doesnt look good, or I cant afford it that day. Buy a little here and there and stock up those cupboards. Would like to know where the zucchini comes from?

PS. I miss when we could comment and ask questions of other reviewers. One person just said "poisonous". Like, what do they even mean by that? I had this a few times and doing well so far :)
text_fidelity_b: Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz

Fizik Performance Bicycle Bar Tape - Soft, Tacky & Classic Professional Bike Handlebar Tape (2mm, 2.7mm, 3mm) This is a review of the updated Fizik Tempo Microtex Classic (2mm) bar tape. I have been using the old Fizik performance 3mm tacky bar tape on both my road and CX/gravel bikes for several years now, and while that tape was pretty difficult to install (especially on irregular bar shapes) I really liked the look and feel of it and the durability.

This 2mm Microtex tape was much easier to wrap my aero bars with compared to the thick and tacky version I have been using.. but I do prefer the feel of the thicker tacky tape. I can't really speak to the durability of this tape since I've only had it for a few rides but it seems durable when installing it and appears to be easy to clean.

Unfortunately it seems Fizik no longer makes perforated 3mm tacky tape, the new iterations are either flat unperforated tape or grooved channels. I'm not a big fan of the grooved look of the Vento tapes but I may consider using the flat Terra version when I need to rewrap my CX bike.. I really wish they would release a tacky version of the Tempo perforated tape though as I much prefer that look.

XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination Since I turned my bike into a commuter vehicle, I've been looking to replace my existing light with a road and pedestrian friendly.

I was looking for a light that had a cutoff like a automotive headlight. I found that there was a standard called STVZO that fell onto that category. I also saw that many of these light were rather expensive. So I was surprised to find this on being that is was fairly inexpensive compare to similar lights.

Comparatively, this one is noticeably larger then my current light. Well, the first thing I tried after taking it out of the box, was to charge it. I plugged in one of my existing USB C cables and could not charge it. My plug was too big to fully seat. I was able to use the cable that was in the packaging. So be aware of that consideration. The port cover fits tightly and takes a little bit of effort to pop open.

I chose the handle bar mount. The mount doesn't rotate laterally and thus not vulnerable to snapping off at the pivot light other handle bar mounted lights.

I have a standard size extender and the mount needs to be tightened all the way to get a good cinch. Unfortunately, that means the long screw sticks up and blocks the light from sliding on. So I need to add some rubber strips to remove the slack.

The manual vs motion mode was a little confusing at first. I opted to go with manual mode to keep it on while I'm at a traffic stop.

Well, the proof us in the pudding. The beam pattern has a clear and distinct cut off. It's also bright and has a good spread. At this price point, this is a great value for a quality light.

Overall, I'm really happy with using this light while riding at night. The issue of the loose mount and small USB port could be improved upon, but it still get's the job done.
text_fidelity_b: XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination

Anyway, it seems like they got everything right, but just be advised that this is NOT the type of case where you can see your phone through the top, despite saying it's compatible with all these devices; that's just a way to add search terms, and I guess it's technically correct that those phones will fit in this bag.

While I haven't had this out in a downpour, it has what appear to be excellent quality, self-sealing zippers on the exterior that should be essentially waterproof as far as rain goes (likely not submersible). It's sort of a "shell" case in that it is semi-rigid, and the material has a checkered carbon fiber look to it, which is neat looking and will likely match a lot of fancier bikes, but will work with anything since it's basically black.

The three straps come large enough that I imagine they can be used with any bike, and can be adjusted down as necessary; I expect the cleanest and nicest installations will involve trimming the excess. The one strap is "across" the opening of the two sections, which would limit how far you can open it, except there is a piece of fabric inside artificially limiting how far you can open it, perhaps so that the former's limitation is not so obvious, but I suspect it will help keep you from dropping stuff out of the case while it is installed on the bike.

One side is a half-height net, and the other side is a full height zippered net, both of which offer some stretch, and are very much like a good piece of luggage.

This definitely adds a little bulk to your bike, and I'm not convinced everyone will want on for permanent storage (there are lots of other placement options to consider), but I can imagine that this goes quite far when doing multi-day riding with camping stops. The great thing is that it can be taken off and put back on quite easily, and as needed.
text_fidelity_b: WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7"

I like tea bottles over cups as I am a lot less likely to spill tea in a bottle versus a cup, so I have several that I keep on my desk. I was interested in trying this tea bottle, and it has worked out well for me so far.

One thing that is different about this bottle is the screen. The screen is located at the bottom of the bottle, not at the top. It also is bigger than most, being slightly larger than a 35mm film tube. The holes in it are small enough to keep larger particles form getting the tea but they are not small enough to keep something like fine tea leaves (or regular ground coffee) out.

The bottle is borosilicate glass and is single layer. So, to compensate for the lack of insulation the bottle comes with a sleeve that keeps you from burning your hand and also helps to keep the contents of the bottle hot (or cold, as appropriate). The sleeve is easy to put on and take off.

The bottle comes with two bottle brushes and a handle for those brushes. The brushes are simply foam heads on a plastic handle but they are sufficient for properly cleaning out the bottle.

So far this bottle has worked out well for me. I am happy with it.

text_fidelity_a:
Kelley Coffey-Meyer's The Shape of Things to Come DVD (also called Complete Cardio Sculpting) This is the first DVD I've tried from instructor Kelly Coffey-Meyer, and I must say that I liked both the workout and Kelly very much. I found it very inspiring that Kelly, who has been involved in fitness for quite a long time, is a mom in her 40s, yet she seemingly had plenty of energy for this tough workout! This DVD contains a 50-minute circuit-style workout which alternates toning work with short cardio intervals. Some of the cardio work uses an optional step, but you could easily modify if you don't have a step (or substitute a small, sturdy stool, as you don't need much width). Kelly also uses two sets of dumbbells, which she labels "light" and "heavy"; I'm still trying to figure out what poundage is best for me, but for now, sticking to 5# the entire way through seems to work fairly well. The time breakdown listed on the DVD case is as follows: Warm-up, 4 minutes, Sculpting and Cardio, 34 minutes, Chest and Abs, 10 minutes, Stretch, 2 minutes.

The warm-up uses mostly basic, familiar moves, but somehow, Kelly makes them seem more fun! She includes knee-ups on the step and ends with some front and side kicks, which I loved. The first sculpting interval comes next and is focused on back/core. Using your "heavy" weights, you'll start with a very functional fitness-oriented "chop" move, first going halfway, then all the way down to the floor. Next comes a v-press, a front pull/press combo, and an underhand/overhand row, with the entire circuit repeated once. The first cardio interval begins with plyo lunges on the step (there is quite a bit of impact throughout the video, but again, it's easily modified), squat, slide, and step-knees. For the second sculpting segment, you'll focus on shoulders, this time using your "light" weights. Kelly begins with a unique side/front staggered raise, moves into a forward raise with upright row, and finishes with side delt raises and a shoulder press; again, the series is repeated. You'll then go back, repeat the previous cardio segment, and then repeat the entire shoulder work sequence once more.

The next cardio segment starts with jumping jacks--I usually hate these, but again, they were fun here! You do two jacks, a slow jack, and then a plyo X--a jump to each side while in a boxer's crouch--before finishing with hamstring curls on the step. The next sculpting interval consists of biceps work: hammer curls, side curls with a slow count down, half-up curls, and front elbow lifts; you then repeat both the jumping jack cardio series and the biceps work. The final cardio choreography has the most impact, and I found it to be the most intense as well. You'll do a wide jog, a skate from side to side, jump rope, and then plyo hops on the step. The last sculpting series works the triceps in several unique ways. First comes French presses and tricep kickbacks, but then you do a move which I've never seen before, sort of like an upright row behind your back, and you finish by lifting your arms straight behind you. The high impact-cardio and triceps work are both repeated.

Are you wondering when the leg work is going to come in? Well, the last standing segment is sort of a cardio sculpting series focused on the lower body. Using your heavy weights and moving very quickly, you'll squat and place both weights on the floor, squat and pick up one weight, squat and pick up the other weight, and then repeat the entire sequence MANY times (you may want to consider starting with lighter weights here). Next, you'll do what Kelly calls "a skater's lunge" but which I've usually seen called a curtsey dip: you'll lunge one leg behind the other on an angle, with the added twist of holding a dumbbell in your opposite hand and touching it to the floor in front of your static foot. You'll do all the reps on one side before moving to the other, then repeat the squat series (I was feeling pretty tired the second time through!), and finally, finish with the skater's lunge, alternating sides this time.

You're not done yet, though--now it's on the the floor for chest/abs work! Kelly lies on the step, but you can lie directly on the floor if needed. The chest series includes chest press, wide-angle chest press, 2-count chest flies, and lower chest/tricep pushes. The abs work was the only part of this video that I found a bit on the boring side, as it's just a simple series of crunches: crunch up, crunch lifting leg in and out, crunch lifting leg in/out and twisting to the side, and repeat on other side. Both the chest and the abs sequences are repeated once. Kelly finishes with quite a very quick stretch. Still lying on the step, she stretches the hamstrings, moves to seated for a chest/back stretch, stretches the neck on both sides, and yes, now you're done!

I really enjoyed this workout--the time flew by, particularly during the cardio intervals, and the toning work was fun, unique, varied, and had a functional fitness flavor (ie, mimicking movements from everyday life such as twisting). I would rate this as a high intermediate workout, but it would probably be doable for advanced beginners by using even lighter weights and going without the step (those wanting more of a challenge can heavy up on the weights if they dare and use a higher step). The DVD is very well-chaptered with various shorter workout options, such as just doing the cardio, completing only a single circuit, etc. Overall a great addition to my video library and highly recommended!
text_fidelity_b: Kelley Coffey-Meyer's The Shape of Things to Come DVD (also called Complete Cardio Sculpting)
